profile.headline: SWE @ Principal Financial
profile.summary:
During my time as a Software Engineer at Capital One, I had the privilege to work on various impactful projects, such as the development of a Micro-Front-End platform built with Vue.js, Node.js, and AWS. This project was structured in a modular format, allowing federated teams to collaborate seamlessly. I also designed a Step-Up Authentication workflow to enhance data security and implemented feature enhancements that resulted in a 55% performance boost and an 80% reduction in build time. Additionally, I engineered test agent servicing tools for a cloud-native test orchestration platform, demonstrating my proficiency in Playwright, Go, and REST Assured.
My ability to optimize software extends beyond development and testing. I applied the Sidecar Design Pattern to testing agents, consolidating post-processing within a single ECS container, achieving a remarkable 75% reduction in test completion time. These experiences have honed my skills in efficient software engineering and collaboration.
As a Software Engineer Intern at Leidos, I led research and development initiatives focused on enhancing security and exploitation capabilities in various operating system environments. Furthermore, I played a pivotal role in the development of Markit, a highly modular web-based platform, demonstrating my versatility in technologies such as Vue.js. The platform empowers users to efficiently collect, organize, and analyze assets within computer systems.
In my previous role at Capital One, I completed Certified Secure Software Engineer Training, with a particular focus on addressing and mitigating insecure code issues. I led the development of a company website, utilizing Angular and AWS S3 to create a comprehensive repository for Cloud and Productivity Engineering information. I also implemented Single Sign-On (SSO) functionality and introduced UI enhancements, showcasing my proficiency in modern web technologies.
My diverse skill set encompasses languages such as Python, TypeScript, C, C#, Java, and SQL, along with proficiency in web frameworks and technologies like Node, React, Angular, Vue, and ASP.Net. I also hold an AWS Solutions Architect certificate.
My academic background, with a BS in Computer Science from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is complemented by the practical experience and awards I've earned during my academic journey.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Charlotte, North Carolina, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Led the technical evaluation and enterprise onboarding of the Conning GEMS economic scenario modeling platform by designing and assessing AWS hosting architectures (EC2/EBS), evaluating security and operational requirements, and partnering with vendor and cross-functional stakeholders to drive solution selection and enterprise Application Risk Assessment (ARA) completion.

Developed scalable full-stack features using Next.js, React, and TypeScript for a cloud-native actuarial modeling and financial reporting platform, improving data accessibility and operational efficiency.

Architected a multi-region disaster recovery solution using Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables and a warm standby strategy, improving resiliency for mission-critical financial systems.

Maintained and enhanced legacy applications, supported production systems through monthly on-call rotations, and resolved critical incident
positions.insights: Skills: Software Design · Next.js · Amazon Web Services (AWS) · React · Disaster Recovery

positions.description:
Contributed to a modular micro-frontend platform using Vue.js, Node.js, AWS Lambda, and Module Federation, enabling independent deployments across multiple engineering teams while improving platform scalability and developer productivity.

Designed and implemented a Step-Up Authentication solution to strengthen application security by introducing risk-based identity verification for sensitive user operations.

Optimized enterprise testing infrastructure by implementing the Sidecar Design Pattern and ECS containerization, reducing CI/CD pipeline execution time by 75% while significantly improving build reliability and scalability
